item.title: Travel, Privacy and Work Rules Shift
item.description: Fresh transport disruptions, privacy rules, work changes and practical service launches lead today’s briefing.
item.content:encoded:
Fresh transport disruptions, privacy rules, work changes and practical service launches create several concrete choices to act on now.

  1. SH6 Makarora–Lake Hāwea reopens only by escorted convoy NZTA will run up to three escorted convoy movements daily from 1 September through the slip-hit section of State Highway 6, which has been closed since Friday after about 30 slips; heavy rain may force another full closure. 31 Aug 2026. NZTA · Follow up
  2. Australia unveils a right to erase platform data Australia released draft privacy reforms that would let people require large social-media platforms and search engines to destroy their personal information, add a “fair and reasonable” data-use test, tighten consent rules, and create myGov IDLock testing later in 2026 before a 2027 rollout. 31 Aug 2026. ABC · Follow up
  3. Queensland now requires licences for e-bikes and e-scooters From 31 August, public riders of e-bikes, e-scooters, e-skateboards and e-unicycles in Queensland must generally be at least 16 and hold a valid learner licence or higher; equivalent overseas licences count, with specified supervision, recreation and medical exemptions. 31 Aug 2026. Queensland Government · Qld transport · Follow up
  4. Thailand tightens Destination Thailand Visa applications Thai missions have tightened DTV supporting documents from 31 August: the London embassy now requires permanent-residence proof in its jurisdiction instead of proof of current location, plus a criminal-record certificate issued within six months, materially reducing the convenience of applying while merely visiting a third country. 31 Aug 2026. Royal Thai Embassy London · DTV change summary · Follow up
  5. Victoria delays its proposed work-from-home right Victoria’s proposed legal right for eligible workers to work from home two days a week will not start on 1 September; Premier Ben Carroll moved the intended commencement to 1 July 2027 while the bill remains under parliamentary consideration. 11 Aug 2026. ABC · Follow up
  6. Melbourne shows concrete Microsoft Fabric hiring demand Multiple Melbourne employers are recruiting for hands-on Microsoft Fabric work: Kinetic is building a new ANZ enterprise data platform, More says it is mid-way through a shift to Fabric, and a global investment manager is offering a 12-month senior Fabric/Power BI data-engineering contract at A$950 a day including super. 20–31 Aug 2026. Kinetic role · More role · Profusion role · Follow up
  7. Australia sets minimum pay floors for app delivery work Australia’s first enforceable minimum-standards order for employee-like on-demand food and grocery delivery workers is now operating, with engaged-time floors of A$31.30 an hour for bicycle/e-scooter work, A$31.50 for motorcycle work and A$32 for car or small-van work, plus required top-ups when earnings fall short. 17 Aug 2026. Fair Work Ombudsman · Follow up
  8. Ring makes stronger video encryption the worldwide default Ring’s new TAKE encryption will roll out in phases from September and become the default for all customers worldwide; each video uses rotating keys that Ring can access temporarily inside a secure enclave for enabled cloud features before the keys are deleted, while end-to-end encryption remains optional. 27 Aug 2026. Amazon · Ring NZ · Follow up
  9. Auckland City Rail Link starts passenger service 13 September Auckland Transport has published first-service details for the completed City Rail Link: passenger trains begin around 5am on Sunday 13 September, with new underground stations and through-running that cuts Panmure–Karanga-a-Hape to about 21 minutes and Glen Innes–Te Waihorotiu to about 15 minutes. 27 Aug 2026. Auckland Transport · CRL · Follow up
  10. New Zealand runway-end safety rules take effect New Civil Aviation Rules took effect on 31 August, aligning runway-end safety-area requirements with ICAO standards and allowing engineered arresting systems; CAA says the change gives regional airports more flexibility and can enable larger passenger aircraft where runway geometry previously constrained development. 31 Aug 2026. CAA · CAA summary · Follow up
  11. Sunbury trains face an open-ended replacement-bus disruption From 1 September, buses replace trains between Watergardens and Sunbury until further notice because of industrial action; services between Watergardens and central Melbourne will run to an altered timetable. 30 Aug 2026. Transport Victoria · Follow up
  12. Google releases Gemini 3.5 Transcribe Google released Gemini 3.5 Transcribe with real-time and recorded-audio transcription, automatic formatting and filler-word cleanup, custom vocabulary, automatic language detection across more than 85 languages, speaker attribution for up to three speakers and word-level timestamps; developers can access it through Gemini APIs. 26 Aug 2026. Google · DeepMind · Follow up
  13. Ask Gemini begins rolling out inside Google Chat Google began a gradual rollout of Ask Gemini in Chat for eligible Workspace plans on 26 August, adding one interface that can search Gmail, Drive and Calendar, catch up conversations, create content, and manage meetings and tasks without leaving Chat. 26 Aug 2026. Google Workspace · Follow up
  14. Star Wars Zero Company is now available EA released the turn-based tactics game Star Wars Zero Company on 27 August; Steam currently shows a Mostly Positive user consensus with about 78% positive English-language reviews, clearing the briefing’s review-quality threshold for a major Star Wars release. 27 Aug 2026. Steam · Follow up
  15. Auckland ferry terminal changes start 1 September Pier 2 at Auckland’s Downtown Ferry Terminal will close from 1 September to early November for electric-ferry charging works, moving Devonport services to Pier 4; a nearby Queens Wharf footpath section will also close until early December. 24 Aug 2026. Auckland Transport · Follow up
  16. Christchurch launches an Aranui–New Brighton trial bus Metro Christchurch started Route 110 on 31 August, running hourly between New Brighton and The Palms via Aranui, Pak’nSave Breezes Road and Burwood Park; the trial is scheduled for 12 months and accepts contactless cards, Metrocard and cash. 31 Aug 2026. Metro Christchurch · Follow up
  17. Kmart’s biggest New Zealand store opens 10 September Kmart will open a 6,700-square-metre, 24-hour Westgate store in Auckland on 10 September, its largest New Zealand location and the country’s first using the retailer’s Plan C+ format. 19 Aug 2026. Inside Retail NZ · Follow up
  18. Tupperware returns to New Zealand after four years Tupperware relaunched in New Zealand on 24 August after ceasing local trading in 2022, with a new local distributor and a full-range e-commerce store; retail partnerships are planned later. 24–25 Aug 2026. Inside Retail NZ · Idealog · Follow up
